Hi everyone!

I’ve recently joined the community :) For context, I’m a final-year CS undergrad working on formalising some first-order online convex optimisation results in Lean 4. While formalising a lemma on projected gradient descent steps, I needed the standard ambient normal cone to a convex set. Here is what I have written up:

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

def NormalCone (K : Set E) (x : E) : Set E :=
  {n : E | ∀ y ∈ K, inner ℝ n (y - x) ≤ 0}

I looked through Mathlib (I saw tangentConeAt in calculus, as well as various cone definitions in Convex.Cone), but couldn't seem to find this standard definition of the normal cone to a set at a point in real inner product spaces. Did I miss an existing definition somewhere in Mathlib, or is it genuinely not there yet? If it's missing, would a small PR adding it alongside basic properties be welcome?

Thanks for reading!

Hi Gustas

I am not very experienced at lean but I am familiar with online convex optimization. I think convex normal cones do not exist in Mathlib. You should check out LML https://github.com/LeanMachineLearning/LML/tree/main. We added subgradients and the normal cone is a special case of it and we hope to add it to mathlib in the future.

You might want to check out my message on OGD and regret proofs here too: #Lean Machine Learning > Formalizing Learning with Expert Advice @ 💬.

Hi, thanks a lot for the pointer! I'm currently checking out LML. Also, thanks for sharing your thread on OGD and the dynamic regret decomposition, it's really spot-on for what I'm looking for. Really appreciate the help! :)
